Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the candid input on the use case and success criteria. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our call:

• Procurement & legal: Alex Murphy (procurement) was mentioned as the gate for PO/contract. Can you confirm his contact and typical procurement timeline?

Attached is a first-pass stakeholder map / mutual action plan (FinPay_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) that captures attendees, owners, and an initial milestone schedule. Ask: can you review and confirm owners and any missing stakeholders by EOD Monday so we can finalize the MAP and drive the next steps?

If that timeline looks broadly correct I can schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the MAP and answers to any security questions.

Thanks — Marissa

Quick internal note — pricing work: I put together two clean options (attached pricing_sheet_v1.xlsx):

Option A (recommended): 12-month committed capacity with a predictable monthly commit and a 10% discount vs list. Lower unit cost and aligns with their request for predictable spend.
Option B: Pay-as-you-go with higher per-token price but zero commit (flexible for unpredictable workloads).

I recommend we lead with Option A as the default and present PAYG as a fallback. I’ll prepare a one-slide summary for the Mar 10 call and highlight contract terms that procurement typically asks about (data residency, liability caps, termination notice).

–Ben
